correctness.rationale: The 2-by-2 Hankel block M=[[conj(a),conj(b)],[conj(b),0]] has exact top singular value L=(|a|+sqrt(|a|²+4|b|²))/2. The kernel formula follows from its first two Taylor coefficients. With u=|b|/L in [0,1], the chosen kernel radius u/2 gives squared testing/output ratio >=(1-u²/4)(1+u⁴/4)=25/27+(8-3u²)(3u²-2)²/432. This proves the universal inequality including zero coefficients and all complex phases. At a=1,b=sqrt(6), strict radial concavity proves the unique maximum at r=1/sqrt(6), giving L=3 and K=5/sqrt(3), so the constant and equality characterization are exact. The 2,621 finite diagnostics reproduce the algebra but are not used as a general proof.

value.rationale: Quadratic symbols are the first nontrivial polynomial family for which SRKT fails and were singled out explicitly as an example in the 2026 motivating article. Determining their exact global kernel-testing loss and all coefficient-modulus equality cases is a natural sharp quantitative classification; the optimum 3sqrt(3)/5 is not a parameter-renaming or a known-table recomputation. The bound provides the exact finite-degree benchmark for testing norm estimates without claiming a universal compact-Hankel theorem.
